title: How to Legally Own Another Person
coreMove: Distinguish formal freedom from practical freedom by locating what the institution can threaten if the person disobeys.
sourcePressure: Employment, status perks, and dependence can create practical ownership even when a person remains formally free.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into a loose rant about jobs or a literal claim that employment equals slavery.

sourceAnchors.name: gyrovague monks
sourceAnchors.detail: The authorized excerpt uses gyrovague monks as a contrast: free people are hard for institutions to domesticate.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The wandering monk is useful because he shows why institutions prefer people with something to lose.

sourceAnchors.name: Coase
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says Coase explains firms through transaction costs while Taleb adds employment as risk management and domestication.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Coase explains why firms exist; the sharper question is why they want people whose future can be held in the firm's hand.

sourceAnchors.name: Roman slaves as treasurers
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar identifies Roman use of slaves as treasurers as a stark case of maximizing downside on the steward to reduce owner risk.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Roman treasurer case turns ownership into incentive design: the steward is reliable because his downside is total.

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity contractor refusing a retainer that would require full-time obedience
exampleSpecs.audience: solo specialist comparing contract freedom against employee dependence
exampleSpecs.stakes: one salary offer could buy his calendar and silence future refusals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire crosses out the exclusivity clause and keeps the right to walk away from bad security advice.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red pen beside a retainer agreement

exampleSpecs.domain: scholarship student avoiding criticism of a lab protocol
exampleSpecs.audience: graduate student whose placement depends on the same adviser she must challenge
exampleSpecs.stakes: a safety concern may be buried because future employability is hostage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco records the failed sterilization test and asks for a second sign-off before the adviser can turn dependency into silence.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chemical smell near a lab sink

exampleSpecs.domain: expat manager with school fees covered by the firm
exampleSpecs.audience: reader in a status-rich assignment that makes dissent expensive
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing perks would uproot family life and identity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida lists every perk she would lose, then separates the policy judgment from the lifestyle leash.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a relocation benefits folder on a hotel desk

exampleSpecs.domain: startup employee asked to publicly defend a roadmap he doubts
exampleSpecs.audience: engineer whose equity and references depend on obedience
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bad product promise could bind customers while the employee stays trapped
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel asks whether contractors are allowed to refuse the promise and notices employees are the only ones expected to defend it.

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal consultant versus staff planner on flood approvals
exampleSpecs.audience: public servant learning why dependence creates reliability for the institution
exampleSpecs.stakes: the institution wants someone who cannot simply leave after saying no
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia compares the consultant's refusal email with the staff planner's revised approval and marks where job fear entered.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rolled flood maps stacked on a cart

exampleSpecs.domain: airline pilot asked to accept a risky scheduling shortcut
exampleSpecs.audience: crew member seeing why contracts alone do not create trust
exampleSpecs.stakes: passenger safety depends on someone with enough independence to refuse
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf asks who loses license, salary, and reputation if the shortcut fails, then rejects the dispatch change.
